objective: Prove: in any network of rule-60 rings joined by left-reading contacts, a contact keeps its two chain-end witnesses at every lag exactly when the weighted closed walks returning to it cancel (D_cc = 1); the positions embed the ring graph in a surface whose rings and faces are the contact graph's closed routes; in a uniform network D_cc = 1 iff every closed-walk count at c is even; an automorphism fixing c and exchanging its rings cancels them, so every orientably regular network (loops, two rings sharing m contacts, the Platonic networks, lattices of rings on a torus) persists at every lag at every size; and a contact joining a two-contact ring to a ring of three or more contacts, with no two-contact face, has exactly one return of length two, so in a uniform network its witnesses lapse.
status: Proved 2026-11-08 (by hand; finite claims checked): in a network of rule-60 rings with law (12,12) contacts a contact keeps its chain-end witnesses at every lag exactly when its returns in the contact graph cancel (D_cc = 1); the positions embed the ring graph in a surface whose rings and faces are the contact graph's closed routes; in a uniform network the returns cancel iff every return count is even; an automorphism fixing a contact and exchanging its rings cancels them, so loops, two rings sharing m contacts, the five Platonic networks and square, triangular and honeycomb lattices of rings on a torus keep every contact persistent at every lag at every size; a contact where a two-contact ring meets a ring of three or more, with no two-contact face, has one unpaired return of length 2, so in a uniform network its witnesses lapse (figure-eights and chords).
title: Symmetry cancels returns; a shared ring with more contacts does not
